source.title: Adversarial Concept Search: Predicting Compositional Errors From Feature Geometry
source.authors: Jennifer Lu; Ruo-Chen Zhang; Isabelle Lee; David Alvarez-Melis; Ellie Pavlick; Naomi Saphra

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains SCAN toy Transformers and measures whether concept-representation interference predicts compositional errors, using a method different from the original toy-superposition setup. It also applies this geometry-to-error analysis to an LLM.
record.gate_note: Results about SCAN representation geometry and compositional accuracy, and LLM compositional accuracy, are included. The paper's cited results from other studies are not rows. Layer choices, variance thresholds, and other values used only to select settings are not rows. The paper does not measure polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery, or whether feature count exceeds dimension.
record.test_reason: The study assumes lossy superposition as its explanation and uses it to build an error predictor, Compositional Interference (CI), from angles between atomic-concept representations. It reports how well CI predicts compositional errors (correlations, PR-AUC) in SCAN toy Transformers and Llama-3.2-3B. It never measures what any version names: feature count versus dimension, sparsity-dependent transitions, polysemantic neurons, capacity allocation, SAE recovery, or feature dimensionality. CI is computed over averaged concept vectors or SVD subspaces, not over recovered superposed features. The authors call superposition an interpretation ('we posit'). This is a related construct, interference predicting errors, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that angular interference (CI) between atomic-concept representations predicts compositional failures in SCAN toy models and in Llama-3.2-3B, without evaluating the composed inputs. They attribute this to lossy superposition, which is posited rather than measured. They note limits: near-saturation regimes, the need for cluster mean-centering, and unmodeled constructive interference.
record.recipe_differences: Trains task-specific SCAN Transformers and measures concept-geometry/error associations, then applies the same general prediction approach to Llama-3.2-3B. It does not reproduce the original toy superposition model's feature-sparsity and importance sweeps or its feature-allocation measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: SCAN CI correlations vary with model dimension and training coverage; the paper reports weaker behavior in near-saturated accuracy regimes. Multihop results change sign depending on cluster mean-centering. The paper also reports that shorter SCAN commands show weaker trends, especially 2-concept examples.

fits_no_version.finding: In SCAN decoder-only Transformers (d=8–64), higher CI between atomic-concept representations correlates with item-level compositional errors in most non-saturated settings. Example: d=64, 4% coverage, r_pb=-0.219. Correlations turn weakly positive in some near-saturated settings (d=12 at 64/80%, d=32 at 80%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Angular interference between atomic-concept representations predicts compositional generalization failures in small Transformers, except near accuracy saturation.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher training coverage yields more pairwise-orthogonal, more isotropic atomic-concept representations in SCAN models (shown in a figure).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Broader compositional training coverage increases orthogonality of concept representations.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3.2-3B, cluster-centered CI predicts multihop and multilingual factual-recall failures (r_pb about -0.08 to -0.29). The multihop sign reverses without centering. Coarse task-level correlations are significant in only some languages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cluster-centered geometry between atomic-concept representations predicts LLM compositional failures, depending on removing background cluster structure.

record.code_released: The authors state they will release code upon the paper decision; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The SCAN runs use a single random seed (42). The paper's direct LLM evaluation is on Llama-3.2-3B. Its claimed superposition mechanism is an interpretation rather than a direct measurement of latent feature storage or decoder interference. Some evidence is reported in figures, and the text notes sensitivity to cluster mean-centering, saturation, and command length.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted alternative interference-metric results (minimum, mean, and maximum similarity) reported in SCAN figures and multilingual/coarse-grained analyses, along with additional figure-only curves and breakdowns. The table 1 first-cell significance markers are detached in the provided flattened text and were not inferred.

untested.parts: Features outnumbering dimensions, sparsity sweeps, phase transition, and regular geometry are not measured. Concept-angle measurements are not feature-superposition measurements.
Neuron polysemanticity and capacity allocation are not measured.
No neuron-distribution or SAE analyses; the authors explicitly avoid SAEs.
A language concept is modeled as a multi-dimensional subspace for convenience, but 1-D versus multi-D features is not tested.

missing.what: SCAN Table 1 cell for d=64 at 80% coverage: r_pb=-0.042, p<0.05 (accuracy 0.999). No row records it.
SCAN average exact-match accuracies per d × coverage, needed to identify the saturated regimes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 labels are removed. The CI–error relationship is a consequence the authors derive from an assumed lossy superposition; it is not a test of toy-model superposition geometry. The coverage list is inconsistent in the text (36% vs 32%). A single seed was used. In the flattened text the first-row *** markers of Table 1 appear above the row; they belong to the 4% values in d=8, 12 and 32.

versions.untested_parts: Tests whether measured concept geometry and interference predict compositional errors in SCAN toy Transformers, and whether training coverage and model dimension relate to that signal. Does not directly count features relative to dimensions, manipulate simultaneous feature sparsity or feature importance, or establish the original superposition model's transition and regular geometric regimes.
Does not measure neuron polysemanticity, dedication of dimensions to important features, or sharing caused by capacity competition.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Does not measure feature distribution across neurons or whether SAE dictionaries recover sparse features. Its residual-stream concept geometry and error prediction are not those measurements.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical representational units.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features. It uses a language subspace in one analysis but does not test which kind constitutes superposed features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SCAN settings with negative CI–correctness correlations, especially reported significant correlations
reader_labels.reason: Higher measured interference generally accompanies lower compositional correctness in these toy networks, and the illustrated representations become more orthogonal with increased training coverage (R01, R03-R07, R09-R11, R15-R17, R20-R24). This supports the tested geometry-to-composition relationship, not the full feature-capacity account.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Near-saturated or high-coverage settings, and small or uncertain correlations
reader_labels.reason: The association is small or absent in some settings, and the paper notes saturation at extreme accuracies; some high-coverage correlations are positive (R02, R08, R14, R16, R18, R23, R24).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: SCAN d=12 at 64% and 80% coverage, and d=32 at 80% coverage
reader_labels.reason: CI has a small but statistically significant positive correlation with correctness in these settings, opposite to the expected negative association (R12, R13, R19).
